pass_a_gloss: [...] so [hard] they endured the persecution, that even in caves and in sinkings of rocks prophets hid, when also Elijah himself was running into a deep desert, and was falling before God saying: Your altars they dug down, your prophets they killed, and I was left alone, and they seek my soul; and he was hearing back toward this at once: I left for myself seven thousand men, who did not bend knee to the Baal. But just as then it was not God who was sending Israel into such terrible unholy deeds, but rather, using their own derangements, they slid down themselves, so indeed again, the God and Father having set before all the salvation through Christ, and thrusting away entirely no one, they slid down willingly toward apostasy, having pushed aside the Redeemer. Therefore God did not push away his people, for he set before [them], as I said, that, if indeed they should choose, to get a share of the salvation through Christ. But if by grace, no longer from works, and the rest. But if by grace, he says, no longer from works, since the grace no longer becomes grace; where, he says, someone might suppose to be approved from works, there surely the name and the thing of the grace will be idle and superfluous; for to the one working, he says, the wage is not reckoned according to grace, but according to debt; therefore if the grace [is] from works, it no longer becomes grace. What then? What Israel seeks after, this it did not hit upon. He said that God did not push away his people; but since it was likely that some would stand up in reply, putting forward surely that thing somewhere and saying: And yet how did God not push away the people, if indeed Israel slid away, even if not into all and wholly, yet as in a portion? For a remnant has been saved, and this according to election; he meets [them] again, and very sensibly, and says: What then? that is, what indeed do I say toward these things? What Israel seeks after, this it did not hit upon, but the election hit upon it, and the rest were hardened; for Israel was seeking the justification from law; then how was it to be justified, he says, the law having perfected no one? Therefore Israel was seeking the justification through type, but did not hit upon it; but those picked out and taken out from the others because of the ready obedience hit upon it; for they have been justified through faith; but the rest have been hardened, that is, the hard and unadmonishable. And David says: Let their table become, and the rest. Let their table become, he says, into a snare, and the following; he brings forward for proof of what he said also a prophetic writing, not of one but of two prophets, for confirmation, so that upon mouth of two and three witnesses every word may stand. For accursed, and very rightly, has their table become, that is, the bad hosting and the rawness which they did upon Christ at the time of being crucified; for to him having thirsted they brought vinegar mixed with gall; for this reason also they were darkened in the mind, and have stooped down, imagining only the things upon earth. I say then, did they stumble so that they might fall? May it not happen. I admire you for the gentleness, O divine Paul, for you handle skilfully the words of the economy [...]
pass_b_english: …was the persecution they endured that prophets even hid in caves and in clefts of the rocks (1 Kings 18:4), at the time when Elijah himself fled into the deep wilderness and fell down before God, saying, “They have torn down your altars, they have killed your prophets, and I alone am left, and they seek my life” (Romans 11:3; 1 Kings 19:10). And at once he heard in answer to this, “I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal” (Romans 11:4; 1 Kings 19:18).

But just as then it was not God who drove Israel into such dreadful impieties, but they slipped down of themselves, following their own folly, so now again, when God the Father set before all the salvation that comes through Christ and thrust no one away at all, they slipped of their own will into apostasy, having pushed aside the Redeemer. So God has not rejected his people (Romans 11:2); for, as I said, he set before them the chance to share in the salvation that comes through Christ, if only they would choose it.

“But if by grace, it is no longer from works,” and the rest (Romans 11:6). “But if by grace,” he says, “it is no longer from works; otherwise grace is no longer grace.” Where, he says, someone supposes that he wins approval from works, there the name and the reality of grace will surely be pointless and superfluous; for, he says, “to the one who works, the wage is not counted as grace but as what is owed” (Romans 4:4). So if grace comes from works, it is no longer grace.

“What then? Israel did not obtain what it seeks” (Romans 11:7). He had said, “God has not rejected his people” (Romans 11:2). But since some were likely to rise up against this, putting forward, no doubt, this objection and saying, “Yet how has God not rejected his people, if Israel has slipped away, even if not entirely and completely, yet at least in part? For a remnant has been saved, and that by election” (Romans 11:5), he meets them again, and very wisely, and says, “What then?”, that is, what do I say to this? “Israel did not obtain what it seeks, but the elect obtained it, and the rest were hardened” (Romans 11:7).

For Israel sought justification from the law; but how, he says, could it be justified, when the law had brought no one to perfection (Hebrews 7:19)? So Israel sought the justification that comes through the type, but did not obtain it; yet those who were picked out and set apart from the rest because of their readiness to obey did obtain it, for they have been justified through faith. But the rest have been hardened, that is, the stubborn and those who would not be corrected.

“And David says, ‘Let their table become a snare,’” and the rest (Romans 11:9; Psalm 69:22). “Let their table become a snare,” he says, and what follows. To prove what he has said he also brings in a prophetic text, and that of not one prophet but two, to confirm it, “so that every word may be established by the mouth of two or three witnesses” (Matthew 18:16; Deuteronomy 19:15). For their table has become accursed, and quite rightly: that is, the cruel welcome and the savagery that they showed toward Christ at the time of his crucifixion; for when he was thirsty, they brought him vinegar mixed with gall (Psalm 69:21; Matthew 27:34). For this reason they were also darkened in mind (Romans 11:10) and are bent down, picturing only the things on the earth.
“I say then, have they stumbled so as to fall? By no means” (Romans 11:11). I admire your gentleness, inspired Paul, for you handle words of wise tact with great skill…

οὕτω τὴν δίωξιν ὑπομεμενήκασιν, ὡς καὶ ἐν σπηλαίοις καὶ πετρῶν καταδύσεσι
κρύπτεσθαι προφήτας, ὅτε καὶ αὐτὸς Ἠλίας ἀνέθει μὲν εἰς βαθεῖαν ἔρημον, προσέπιπτε
δὲ τῷ Θεῷ λέγων Τὰ θυσιαστήριά σου κατέσκαψαν, τοὺς προφήτας σου ἀπέκτειναν,
κἀγὼ ὑπελείφθην μόνος, καὶ ζητοῦσι τὴν ψυχήν μου· ἀντήκουε δὲ πρὸς τοῦτο εὐθύς
Κατέλιπον ἐμαυτῷ ἑπτακισχιλίους ἄνδρας οἵτινες οὐκ ἔκαμψαν γόνυ τῇ Βάαλ. ἀλλ'
ὥσπερ τότε Θεὸς μὲν οὐκ ἦν ὁ ταῖς οὕτω δειναῖς ἀνοσιουργίαις ἐνιεὶς τὸν Ἰσραὴλ, ἰδίαις
δὲ μᾶλλον ἀπονοίαις χρώμενοι κατώλισθον αὐτοὶ, οὕτω δὴ πάλιν προθέντος ἅπασι τοῦ
Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς τὴν διὰ Χριστὸν σωτηρίαν, διωθουμένου δὲ παντελῶς οὐδένα,
κατώλισθον ἐθελοντὶ πρὸς ἀπόστασιν, παρωσάμενοι τὸν λυτρωτήν. οὐκ 239 οῦν οὐκ
ἀπώσατο ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ, προὔθηκε γὰρ, ὡς ἔφην, τὸ εἴπερ ἕλοιντο μεταλαχεῖν
τῆς διὰ Χριστοῦ σωτηρίας. Εἰ δὲ χάριτι, οὐκ ἔτι ἐξ ἔργων κ.τ.λ. Εἰ δὲ χάριτί φησιν οὐκ ἔτι
ἐξ ἔργων, ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις οὐκ ἔτι γίνεται χάρις· ἔνθα, φησὶν, ἂν οἴοιτό τις ἐξ ἔργων
εὐδοκιμεῖν, ἐκεῖ δὴ πάντως εἰκαῖον ἔσται καὶ περιττὸν τὸ τῆς χάριτος ὄνομά τε καὶ
χρῆμα· "Τῷ γὰρ ἐργαζομένῳ, φησὶν, "ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν, ἀλλὰ κατὰ
ὀφείλημα·" οὐκοῦν εἰ ἐξ ἔργων ἡ χάρις, οὐκ ἔτι γίνεται χάρις. Τί οὖν; ὃ ἐπιζητεῖ Ἰσραὴλ,
τούτου οὐκ ἐπέτυχεν. Ἔφη μὲν ὅτι "οὐκ ἀπώσατο ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ·" ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἦν
εἰκὸς ἀνταναστῆναί τινας, ἐκεῖνό που πάντως προϊσχομένους καὶ λέγοντας Καίτοι πῶς
οὐκ ἀπώσατο τὸν λαὸν ὁ Θεὸς, εἴπερ ἀπώλισθεν ὁ Ἰσραὴλ, εἰ καὶ μὴ εἰς ἅπαν καὶ
ὁλοτελῶς, ἀλλ' οὖν ὡς ἐν μοίρᾳ; λεῖμμα γὰρ σέσωσται, καὶ τοῦτο κατ' ἐκλογήν· ὑπαντᾷ
δὲ πάλιν καὶ μάλα ἐμφρόνως καί φησι Τί οὖν; τουτέστι, τί δὴ πρὸς ταῦτά φημι; Ὃ
ἐπιζητεῖ Ἰσραὴλ, τούτου οὐκ ἐπέτυχεν, ἡ δὲ ἐκλογὴ ἐπέτυχεν, οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ἐπωρώθησαν·
ἐπεζήτει μὲν γὰρ ὁ Ἰσραὴλ τὴν ἐκ νόμου δικαίωσιν· εἶτα πῶς ἦν δικαιοῦσθαι αὐτὸν,
φησὶ, τετελειωκότος οὐδένα τοῦ νόμου; οὐκοῦν τὴν διὰ τύπου δικαίωσιν ἐπεζήτει μὲν ὁ
Ἰσραὴλ, οὐκ ἐπέτυχε δέ· ἀλλ' οἵ γε ἀπολέγδην καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἐξῃρημένοι διὰ τὸ
εὐπειθὲς ἐπέτυχον· δεδικαίωνται γὰρ διὰ πίστεως· πεπώρωνται δὲ οἱ λοιποὶ, τουτέστιν
οἱ σκληροί τε καὶ ἀνουθέτητοι. 240 Καὶ ∆αβὶδ λέγει Γενηθήτω ἡ τράπεζα αὐτῶν κ.τ.λ.
Γενηθήτω φησὶν ἡ τράπεζα αὐτῶν εἰς παγίδα, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς· παρακομίζει πρὸς ἀπόδειξιν
ὧν εἶπε καὶ γράμμα προφητικὸν, οὐχ ἑνὸς ἀλλὰ δύο προφητῶν πρὸς σύστασιν, "ἵνα ἐπὶ
στό"ματος δύο καὶ τριῶν μαρτύρων σταθῇ πᾶν ῥῆμα." ἐπάρατος γὰρ καὶ μᾶλα ὀρθῶς
γέγονεν αὐτῶν ἡ τράπεζα, τουτέστιν ἡ κακοξενία καὶ ἡ ὠμότης, ἣν ἐπὶ Χριστῷ
πεποίηνται κατὰ τὸν τοῦ σταυροῦσθαι καιρόν· δεδιψηκότι γὰρ αὐτῷ προσεκόμισαν ὄξος
χολῇ συμμιγές· διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἐσκοτώθησαν τὸν νοῦν καὶ κάτω κεκύφασι μόνα
φανταζόμενοι τὰ ἐπὶ γῆς. Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἔπταισαν ἵνα πέσωσι; μὴ γένοιτο. Ἄγαμαί σε τῆς
ἐπιεικείας, ὦ θεσπέσιε Παῦλε, μεταχειρίζῃ γὰρ εὐτεχνῶς τῆς οἰκονομίας τοὺς λόγους·

review_notes: Existing book row (not a placeholder) had several real errors. Wrong sense: διωθουμένου δὲ παντελῶς οὐδένα was 'no one being persecuted' (it means God thrust no one away); οἵ γε ἀπολέγδην… ἐξῃρημένοι διὰ τὸ εὐπειθές was 'those who were cast out from the others through being lawless' (it means those picked out and set apart for their readiness to obey; doctrine reversed); ἐπάρατος… γέγονεν αὐτῶν ἡ τράπεζα was 'has become a snare' (it is 'has become accursed'); μὴ ἔπταισαν ἵνα πέσωσι was 'did they fall in order to perish' (stumble… fall). Wrong agency: τετελειωκότος οὐδένα τοῦ νόμου was 'no one had completed the law' (the law perfected no one; Hebrews 7:19); ἀντήκουε was 'God answered' (Elijah heard in answer). Join: οὕτω…ὡς with δύσοιστον from u09-rem-close was mistranslated as 'Thus they endured… prophets hiding'. Omission: the reply clause ὑπαντᾷ δὲ πάλιν… φησι Τί οὖν; τουτέστι, τί δὴ πρὸς ταῦτά φημι was dropped, and the objection was given as Cyril's own statement; δεδιψηκότι ('when he was thirsty') was dropped. Addition: 'for if it is from works' before 'grace is no longer grace' (ἐπεί = 'otherwise'). Other: ἀπονοίαις was 'intentions' (folly); 'God and Father' for 'God the Father'; ungrammatical 'He offered, as I said, if they would take a share'; 'oh divine Paul' archaic; 'words of economy' a calque (οἰκονομία here is Paul's tactful handling, praised with ἐπιεικεία). Scripture: Psalm 69:23 corrected to Psalm 69:22 (LXX 68:23); inline citations added for Romans 11:2–11, 4:4, 1 Kings 18:4, 19:10, 19:18, Hebrews 7:19, Psalm 69:21, Matthew 27:34, Deuteronomy 19:15. Divine pronouns set to lower case to match the book. Title changed to name the thought. Note: this row's translator_notes quote the old opening and closing words ('…Thus they endured...', 'words of economy') and should be updated when the fix is applied.
